title.narrative: Output 2.2. Increased capacity of Member States to apply international labour standards

description.narrative: DWCP 2018-2022 (extended till 2027 in 2022) includes references to the actions guided by the recommendations of the ILO supervisory bodies. DWCP Output 2.2.1 refers to improving the responsiveness of the Department of Labour in dispute settlement; DWCP Output 2.2.2 - refers to strengthening the capacity of constituents to respond to the comments of the ILO supervisory bodies; application of ratified standards as guided by the recommendation of the supervisory bodies; DWCP outcome 2.3 - refers to the labour law reform guided by comments of the ILO supervisory bodies. ILO developed the draft DWCP 2018-2022 and facilitated tripartite consultations on the DWCP. In 2022 ILO facilitated a tripartite discussion on the extension of the DWCP, the decision to extend the DWCP till 2027 was taken after tripartite consultations because it remained relevant

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour and Foreign Employment (MoLFE) submitted seven out of eight reports due in 2022 (C011, C087, C098, C100, C111, C135, C144) before 1 September 2022 and provided replies to the comments of the ILO supervisory bodies. MoLFE submitted reports due for 2023 on C018, C029, P029, C045, C081, C095, C103, C105, C106, C115, C122, C131, C138, C160, C182 in 2023 responding to the comments of the ILO supervisory bodies before 1 September 2023. ILO organized a workshop in November-December 2022 to strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Labour and Foreign Employment officials and social partners to prepare informative reports to the CEACR, responding to the comments of the supervisory bodies. ILO supported creation of the Ministry of Labour and Foreign Employment inter-ministerial ILS committee and the development of a work plan for 2022-2023 to work with reports to the CEACR and comments of the ILO supervisory bodies. In March 2023 ILO conducted a meeting with the ILS committee to discuss the work on CEACR comments and the development of the reports to the CEACR due in 2023. Three representatives from Sri Lanka participated in the ITC International Labour Standards Academy (Asia and the Pacific) in May 2022; three representatives participated in the ITC training “Best practices in ILS reporting” in March-May 2023.
